title: Knowledge Check 1 - Lessons 1-5
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 1-5 - Solution Positioning. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: A new consultant is asked to describe, in order, the stages data moves through in Data 360. Which sequence is correct?
options: Connect Data, Harmonize and Unify, Analyze and Act
Harmonize and Unify, Connect Data, Analyze and Act
Analyze and Act, Connect Data, Harmonize and Unify
Connect Data, Analyze and Act, Harmonize and Unify
questions.explanation: Data always starts with Connect Data, then Harmonize and Unify, then Analyze and Act. The strongest distractor swaps the first two steps, but you cannot harmonize data that has not been connected.

questions.question: After a stream runs, where do the ingested rows land first, and what is the standardized layer called?
options: A data model object, then a data lake object
A data lake object, then a data model object after mapping
A data graph, then a segment
A unified profile, then a calculated insight
questions.explanation: Ingested rows land in a data lake object, and you map DLO fields to a DMO to harmonize them, so the correct order is DLO then DMO. The first option reverses the order, and a data graph is a precomputed view, not a landing zone.

questions.question: Which statement about a unified profile is correct?
options: It overwrites the source records with the winning values
It is a set of keys that links matching records without changing source data
It only holds fields from a single source
It is created by a data transform, not by identity resolution
questions.explanation: Identity resolution links records into a unified profile and never overwrites source data, while reconciliation only decides what displays. The first option confuses reconciliation with a golden-record overwrite, which is not how Data 360 works.

questions.question: A services organization wants one customer view shared by sales, service, and marketing, plus trusted context for its AI agents. Which positioning statement is correct?
options: Data 360 is a marketing-only CDP
Data 360 is the Salesforce-native data platform that unifies data and powers AI across sales, service, marketing, and commerce
Data 360 is a data warehouse that stores all raw enterprise data
Data 360 is a business intelligence tool
questions.explanation: Data 360 is Salesforce-native and spans functions plus Agentforce grounding. The strongest distractor limits it to marketing, which is exactly the positioning mistake that undersells the platform.

questions.question: Which statement about Data 360 consumption is TRUE?
options: Credits are unlimited once the product is licensed
Data 360 is consumption-based: actions generate usage events that consume credits by usage type
Credits are consumed only for data storage
Flex Credits cannot be used for Data 360 work
questions.explanation: Pricing is consumption-based and each action has a usage type that decrements credits. Flex Credits are interchangeable across Data 360 and Agentforce, so the last option is wrong.

questions.question: An enterprise has five Salesforce orgs and wants one governed Data 360 instance. Which approach does Salesforce recommend?
options: Buy five Data 360 licenses, one per org
Use Data Cloud One with one home org hosting Data 360 and the other orgs as companion orgs
Federate all five orgs with Zero Copy instead of licensing Data 360
Replicate Data 360 metadata manually between orgs
questions.explanation: Each org can hold only one Data 360 license and Salesforce recommends Data Cloud One for multiple orgs, so one home org with companion orgs is the pattern. The first option multiplies cost and fragments governance.

questions.question: Which Einstein Trust Layer capability ensures that a third-party large language model provider neither trains on nor retains your prompts and data?
options: Prompt defense
Zero data retention
Toxicity detection
Platform encryption
questions.explanation: Zero data retention is the Trust Layer guarantee that no data is used for training and nothing is retained by the third-party model. Prompt defense limits harmful or injected outputs but does not govern retention, which is the strongest distractor's mistake.

questions.question: A team wants an AI agent to answer questions from internal PDFs and support transcripts. Through which Data 360 capability are those documents made retrievable at prompt time?
options: Calculated insights
Retrieval augmented generation over a vector database
Segment activation
Identity resolution
questions.explanation: Unstructured files are chunked, vectorized into a vector database, and retrieved to ground prompts, which is retrieval augmented generation. Calculated insights compute metrics from structured data and do not index documents.

questions.question: Which statement about Data 360 grounding for generative AI is correct?
options: Grounding ignores user permissions because the model runs outside Salesforce
Secure data retrieval merges grounding data while preserving the running user's permissions and field-level security
Only structured data can ground a prompt
Grounding requires copying all data into the model
questions.explanation: Dynamic grounding with secure data retrieval honors the running user's permissions and field-level security. The first option is the classic wrong belief, and the Trust Layer is built specifically to preserve those controls.

questions.question: A data scientist connects a churn model built on an external platform to Data 360. After saving the model in AI Models, predictions do not appear in Flow. What is the most likely cause?
options: The model needs to be retrained
The model has not been activated
Bring Your Own Model does not support Flow
The model must be rebuilt in Model Builder
questions.explanation: A saved model is only ready for activation, and predictions are consumable only after activation. Retraining or rebuilding is unnecessary, and BYOM outputs can be consumed by Flow and Apex.

questions.question: Which capability lets a no-code admin build a predictive model using Data 360 data with clicks rather than code?
options: Bring Your Own Model
Model Builder
Retrieval augmented generation
Streaming data transform
questions.explanation: Model Builder builds and trains a predictive model with clicks using Data 360 data. Bring Your Own Model connects an already-built external model, which still requires external data science work.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Bring Your Own Model in AI Models?
options: It retrains external models inside Data 360
It runs inference against an externally trained model, exposing harmonized Data 360 data without moving it
It removes the need for any data science skills
It replaces calculated insights
questions.explanation: BYOM connects an external model endpoint and exposes harmonized Data 360 data for inference without duplicating data. It does not retrain the model or remove the need for data science.

questions.question: A retailer wants to recommend products on its website based on a shopper's recent browsing and cart events within the same session. Which Data 360 capability set best fits?
options: Batch segmentation activated to email
Real-time identity resolution, real-time calculated insights, and real-time actions
A monthly calculated insight and a dashboard
Zero Copy federation alone
questions.explanation: In-session personalization needs real-time identity resolution to merge devices, real-time insights to compute scores, and real-time actions to respond. Batch segmentation is the strongest distractor but it is far too slow for in-session decisions.

questions.question: A service team wants to see the full cross-channel history of a customer on the service console record. Which initial use case is this?
options: A calculated insight on lifetime value
A unified Customer 360 profile surfaced in the console
Advertising suppression
Zero Copy federation of a warehouse
questions.explanation: Showing unified cross-channel history to an agent is the Customer 360 profile use case. A lifetime value insight is a component you could add, but it is not the core of the console view.

questions.question: Which prerequisite most often blocks an initial use case from working?
options: The org has too many users
The unifying entity is not mapped and unified, so the profile does not exist
The data is stored in a data lake
The segment has too few members
questions.explanation: Use cases built on profiles or segments require the entity, Individual or Account, to be mapped to the Customer 360 Data Model and unified. Data location does not block Data 360, which handles lakes through federation.
